title: Chinese Carmakers Overtake Japanese Rivals in Europe
paragraphs: Chinese carmakers have overtaken Japanese brands in European sales for the first time over a full quarter, marking a major shift in the region's automotive market.

According to market research firm Dataforce, Chinese brands accounted for 12.7% of new-car registrations between July and September 2026, compared with 11.9% for Japanese manufacturers including Toyota, Nissan and Honda.
Registrations of Chinese cars roughly doubled year on year, with their market share hitting a record 14.5% in September, up almost three percentage points from August.

Just five years ago, Chinese brands held barely 1% of the European market. Japanese manufacturers, meanwhile, have spent several decades establishing themselves there. Toyota, for example, has sold cars in Europe since 1963.
Much of China's surge has been driven by competitively priced hybrid vehicles, which have become increasingly appealing to European buyers as fuel prices rise.
Brands such as BYD and Chery have been particularly successful. In the UK, Chery's Jaecoo 7 SUV was the country's best-selling car in both March and September.

And while European manufacturers still dominate the region, competition is intensifying in Europe, as well as in China. In what has traditionally been one of the biggest markets for European carmakers, buyers in China are increasingly choosing domestically made vehicles.
On October 29, Volkswagen reported a $6.6 billion third-quarter loss, compared with $1.2 billion a year earlier — its worst quarterly result in more than a decade.
The results add pressure as Volkswagen restructures to cut costs. The company plans to eliminate up to 100,000 jobs by 2030, while four of its German factories face possible closure.
"We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act quickly and decisively," said Volkswagen's finance chief, Arno Antlitz.

Meanwhile, the European Union has introduced additional tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles and is considering further restrictions on hybrid imports. It's also weighing new rules that would favor locally manufactured cars when awarding subsidies and other incentives.
However, Chinese manufacturers are already preparing to produce more cars in Europe. BYD is nearing completion of a factory in Hungary, while Chery is preparing production in Barcelona, Spain.
